rawContent: The #CC19 plenary now shifts to a panel on #metoo with a focus on the abuse of LGBTQI children of color. The discussion opens by mentioning how Kevin Spacey and Bryan Singer have hidden behind their sexualities to defend against allegations of assault.

Pandora just served up the 1998 classic "When The Lights Go Out." My first thought was, "Wow, I haven't heard this in forever."

My second thought was, "Wow, this does not hold up well in the #MeToo/Kavanaugh era."

https://t.co/eIBh7xosjX

Oh wow, this is a bad take.

The #MeToo moment is about women being believed and finally having the societal support to disclose how they've been mistreated.

It's *not* about the men they topple being "victims" deserving of a sympathetic portrayal.
